about: The world map (OpenAI image generation through Codex CLI): the region from above, without lettering; pins and routes in source/world-map.json. Original in ~/Documents/living-tabletop-world-art/.

map.prompt:
Generate one image and save it as glass-republic--world-map.png in the current directory.

A world map for a tabletop role-playing campaign, landscape 3:2, seen straight from above like a hand-painted illustrated map (orthographic top-down view, no perspective, no horizon, no sky). An illustrated plan of a small glass city seen straight from above: pale stone arcades and slate roofs in smoke grey and slate blue, touches of coloured glass. A wide paved parade square fills the centre. On its west side, a grand pale stone hall with a small dome; its roof is cut away to show a long ballroom with two rows of columns, and a long glass-fronted balcony on its east face overlooks the square beside a broad stair. Along the north side of the square runs a high arcaded gallery crowned with frames of coloured glass. At the east end of the square, a rehearsal yard of banner stands and a wooden platform. On the south edge, a corner teahouse with tall double windows. In the bottom left, a dense service quarter with a narrow courier office, and left of it a bathhouse with deep blue windows round a courtyard. In the upper left corner, a walled drill yard with crossbow racks under a long shed. A slow canal curves down the right side; in the upper right a low-walled garden with a round pavilion opens onto it, and a stone stair-street descends east from the garden to a canal quay with a meeting shed and moored boats, right of centre. No people, no text.

Draw every place described above as a small, clearly recognisable landmark exactly at its stated position, with the roads, paths, corridors or waterways between them visible, so that markers can later be pinned on each landmark. Fill the whole picture edge to edge with the mapped land (no border, no frame, no cartouche, no legend, no compass rose, no scale bar, no grid). Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels or symbols that read as letters anywhere on the map. No people, no creatures, no figures.

The attached image is this campaign's cover: match its painting technique, palette, light and mood, but not its composition.

Match one consistent house style: original premium illustrated political-intrigue fantasy for adult audiences only (21+), painterly oil and gouache with restrained ink lines, crisp readable silhouettes and a muted, slightly desaturated finish; Vitrazh, a small city republic whose capital lives behind glass: tall double-paned windows, pale stone arcades and wrought-iron balconies over a wide parade square by a slow canal, a high gallery of signal frames holding large panes of coloured glass, stained-glass light falling in soft coloured patches across stone, parquet and faces, long regimental banners of plain colour fields hanging from poles and railings; palette of smoke grey and slate blue, cold window-glass silver, deep ink black, worn brass and copper, faded banner crimson, bottle green, cobalt blue and milky white glass, with warm candle-gold accents; the quiet tension of polite threats, watchful eyes and closed doors; every person shown is clearly a mature adult. Weapons are only blades, spears, axes and crossbows, kept lowered or sheathed; no firearms, no guns, no gunpowder, no cannons, none exist in this world. Banners and glass panes show only plain colour fields and simple geometric shapes; papers, letters, seals and notices carry only blank or illegible marks. No gore, no blood, no wounds, no corpses, no executions, no torture, no anatomy, no weapons pointed at the viewer. No franchise references, no anime look, no photorealism. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border.
